_comment: HMTc computed-style acceptance spec. Values are the design canon (docs/design-canon/) adapted to the cert palette (#9f2727 accent, not the Index's #8b2a4a). Assertions run on the RENDERED page via tools/check-v3.mjs — never against source SCSS. Grow this file whenever a page's presentation changes (CONTENT-RULES.md §3.5), including `absent: true` for markup that was removed.

/.note: the brand-control hero remains in the canonical display serif.
the primary homepage action is Private Readiness, not a strictness explainer or direct external application.
the global action is Check readiness.

/readiness.note: the on-device readiness decision tool is mounted once, before the explanatory article.
the private starting point remains a six-question check.
the decision map is hidden until a complete form is submitted.
the evidence-reuse destination uses Quartz's generated heading anchor without exposing source syntax.
the page rail links to the rendered evidence-reuse heading.
the readiness surface contains no bold markup.

/category-readiness.note: one generated row per authoritative category state.

/mark.note: public previews do not expose production artwork as a self-service license.

/portal.note: the control-room specimen is explicitly nonfunctional.

/brands.note: the public directory does not invent certificate holders before any exist.

/verify.note: lookup remains visibly inactive until the first certificate exists.

/articles/lead-and-cadmium-in-dark-choco.note: the citation marker is the burgundy accent, NOT the blue link colour. If this reads #1c43ad an older internal-link rule is winning — delete it, do not out-specify (FIDELITY §1).
the PDF-edition download is no longer inline in the reading surface; the generators emit `pdf:` frontmatter and NO body card (CONTENT-RULES §3.5 presentation change).
the Download PDF affordance now lives in the right rail (Rail.tsx PdfCard), driven by the page's `pdf` frontmatter — one home for it sitewide.
the citation-detail panel (SourceCitationPanel) is mounted in the rail; citationPanel.inline.ts fills and reveals it on inline-citation click.
the panel is hidden until a citation is clicked.

/standards/infant-formula-powder.note: canonical burgundy table head. If not burgundy, a duplicate .wiki-content table rule is winning — delete the loser (FIDELITY §1), never out-specify.
no-bold rule (CONTENT-RULES §7): <strong>/<b>/** render at normal weight.
no inline bold on the reading surface. tools/design-lint.mjs blocks this at build; this is the rendered backstop.

/regulations/eu-2023-915.note: the sitewide sticky top-bar; a regulation reference page carries the same chrome as every content page (v3 is not type-gated).
the burgundy record-of-law hero band. The #9f2727 accent must survive the cascade here and at the table head.
the 'Regulation reference' KIND badge (HeroBand, type: regulation).
hero title is the Lora display serif.
the one canonical limits table. A regulation page renders exactly one <thead> (grouped-by-analyte maximum levels).
canonical burgundy table head. If not burgundy, a duplicate .wiki-content table rule is winning — delete the loser (FIDELITY §1), never out-specify.
table-head labels are white on burgundy.
table-head labels are the mono UI face (COMPONENTS §1).
no inline bold on the reading surface. tools/design-lint.mjs blocks this at build; this is the rendered backstop.
the 'On this page' rail sticks below the top-bar.
the Index-only citation/evidence-packet widget must stay absent from the certification site

a reference page RECORDS law; it carries no inline citation superscripts (unlike a briefing/article). The citation-marker COLOUR canon (#9f2727, not link blue) is asserted on /articles, the surface that cites. If a sup.hmtc-cite appears here, a bracketed [N] leaked into transcribed provision text — investigate the register export, do not restyle.

/regulations.note: the register index carries the same burgundy hero band as an instrument page.
the 'Record of law' KIND badge (HeroBand, type: regulation-index).
